clue.text: Animals heading away a tad agitated, they're naturally spotted

indicators.note: agitated letters are shaken up and rearranged
the word Animals loses its head, the leading letter, which goes away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of some nervous creatures, with a nod to the fact that certain beasts are born with spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading away' drops the first letter of Animals to leave NIMALS; 'agitated' shuffles NIMALS with A and TAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed of dog famous for its black or liver spots on a white coat is a fair example of things spotted by nature.

clue.text: Avoided being overheard in Tube

indicators.note: something overheard is caught by ear, so the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to avoid a blow is to duck it, so avoided means ducked

explanation.surface: Someone escaped eavesdroppers by travelling on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' looks like the London Underground but is the plain definition, a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A channel or pipe carrying fluid, as in a tear or air conduit, is a tube.

clue.text: Appear comparatively stupid, without degree in mind

parts.note: to appear a certain way is to look it

indicators.note: without means the degree letter is left out of the word

parts.note: daft means stupid, so more stupid is dafter

explanation.surface: Someone looks sillier for lacking a university qualification.
explanation.definitionFit: To mind children or a shop is to tend or take care of them, a common idiom.

clue.text: Cancel year in French university, being employed by uncle regularly

parts.note: an is the French word for year

indicators.note: the university is taken into the service of the letters, so it sits inside them
regularly takes every other letter of the word uncle

explanation.surface: A student's French year abroad is called off, though an uncle uses the university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks N and L from uncle, and 'being employed by' sets U between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a contract or marriage is to declare it void, which is to cancel it.

clue.text: Scales of charges Spain introduced for third of Catalans

indicators.note: Spain's letter is brought in to stand in place of another letter

parts.note: to charge someone formally with a crime is to indict them, so charges is indicts

indicators.note: third of takes the third letter of the word Catalans

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A list of fees, with Spain introduced in place of some Catalan element, as if about regional politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third of Catalans' is T; 'introduced for' swaps that T in INDICTS for E.
explanation.definitionFit: Scales of measurement, such as price or wage scales, are indexes or plural index figures.

clue.text: Indifferent state in which vehicle's left parked

definitions.text: state in which vehicle's left parked
definitions.meaning: the gear position, out of drive, in which a car is commonly left standing

explanation.surface: An uncaring mood, then the gear position of a stationary car.
explanation.definitionFit: Being impartial means taking no side; a parked car often sits out of gear in the position with no drive engaged.

clue.text: Eat ravenously when course is over

indicators.note: over here means turned over, so the word for course is read backwards

parts.note: a course of water is its flow

explanation.surface: Someone bolts their food once the meal course has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' looks like a meal course, but it is the course of a river, its flow.
explanation.definitionFit: To wolf food is the idiom for gobbling it down greedily, like a hungry beast.

clue.text: Patience, perhaps, Delaware police partly used up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read bottom to top, backwards
partly means only part of the words Delaware police is taken

explanation.surface: Someone's patience with the Delaware police is partly exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patience' is not a virtue here but the Gilbert and Sullivan comic operetta, hence 'perhaps' marking an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is one of the Gilbert and Sullivan comic stage works, so it exemplifies a sung drama.

clue.text: Stick with garden gnome? It might draw many a barb

definitions.text: Stick with garden gnome? It might draw many a barb

parts.words: Stick with garden gnome? It might draw many a barb
parts.note: the classic garden gnome sits by a pond holding an angler's pole; a barb is both a hook point and a kind of fish it might pull in

explanation.surface: Someone holding a stick beside a garden gnome attracts many critical remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barb' reads as a cutting remark, but it is the fish (or the hook's point).
explanation.definitionFit: The angler's pole is the stick a garden gnome traditionally holds, and it reels in fish such as barbs.

clue.text: Location near Manchester, not right place for soup ingredients

indicators.note: not means the letter for right is left out

parts.note: Stockport is a town just south of Manchester

explanation.surface: A town near Manchester is said to be the wrong place to source soup ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: STOCKPORT is a town in Greater Manchester, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A large pan for simmering bones and vegetables into broth holds the makings of soup.

clue.text: Sign of future king's personal honour

parts.note: CR, Charles Rex, was the royal cypher awaiting the then Prince Charles
something personal is one's own

explanation.surface: A token of a prince's private distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: When this was set Charles was heir; CR (Charles Rex) would be his royal cypher as king.
explanation.definitionFit: To honour someone with a title or victory is to crown them, a verb sense of the word.

clue.text: Oldest bus around, certainly …

indicators.note: around means the letters of Oldest bus are moved about

explanation.surface: A claim that the oldest bus around is surely the one in question, trailing into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is without doubt means it is surely so, a synonym for certainly.

clue.text: … transport that's highly regarded by guy motoring organisation retired

parts.note: a guy is a rope or wire holding something steady, a cable

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: Continuing the bus clue: a form of transport admired by a man whose motoring club has retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'highly regarded' seems to mean esteemed, but it means seen up high, overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin hauled along an overhead wire is transport viewed from below, up in the air.

clue.text: Fur, source of insulation for mammal

parts.note: an animal's fur is its coat

indicators.note: source of means the first letter of the word insulation

explanation.surface: A fur garment is a source of warmth for an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring-tailed raccoon relative of the Americas is a member of this warm-blooded animal class.

clue.text: Scud came to ground as usual

indicators.note: ground means crushed and reworked, so the letters of Scud came to are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scud missile came down to earth, as such missiles commonly do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to ground' reads as falling to earth; 'to' is fodder and 'ground' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: What one is used to is customary, the normal or habitual state of things.

clue.text: Lacking energy, attractive girl produces weapon

indicators.note: lacking means the energy letter is missing from the word

parts.note: an attractive person is cute
E is the physics symbol for energy
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A tired pretty girl pulls out a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A short curved sword once favoured by sailors and pirates is a bladed arm.

clue.text: Recommend a romantic partner to entertain very old Conservative

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so these letters hold the others inside

parts.note: the person one goes out with is one's date

explanation.surface: Suggesting a partner for a romantic evening with an elderly Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate a policy is to speak in favour of it, to urge it on others.

clue.text: Round rugby player, one tweeting regularly?

parts.note: a round of a track is a lap
a wing is a rugby player in an outside position

explanation.surface: A heavyset rugby player who is always on social media.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tweeting' suggests posting online, but means birdsong.
explanation.definitionFit: A plover that calls often, the peewit, is a bird that tweets; the question mark flags the social-media misdirection.

clue.text: European, heartily sick over Spanish, English and German articles

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the rest
heartily means taking the heart, the central letters, of sick

parts.note: el is the Spanish definite article
an is an English indefinite article
der is a German definite article

explanation.surface: A European feels very ill after reading Spanish, English and German grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' covers all three: EL, AN and DER.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the North Atlantic island nation of Reykjavik is a European.

clue.text: Interpret tune discovered by classical composer

indicators.note: dis-covered means the covers, the outer letters, are taken off tune

parts.note: Maurice Ravel was a French composer of classical music

explanation.surface: Someone analyses a melody uncovered by a classical musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' looks like found, but means with its cover removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To work out or solve a mystery is to untangle it, so to make sense of it.

clue.text: Rascal active politician stops to ridicule

indicators.note: stops means plugs, so these letters are placed inside the other word

parts.note: a loon is a rogue or idle rascal
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A rogue blocks an energetic MP from mocking someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To satirise or mock a person in writing is the verb meaning to ridicule.

clue.text: Fancy red coat in 1920s style

indicators.note: fancy means ornate or reworked, so the letters of red coat are rearranged

explanation.surface: An elaborate red coat in the fashion of the Jazz Age.
explanation.definitionFit: The geometric decorative movement of the interwar years flourished in that decade.

clue.text: Paper supporting American in dispute

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed below and holding up the other piece

parts.note: tissue is thin paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper backing an American in a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for a matter being argued over or under debate.

clue.text: Assistant ultimately in charge is occupied by work matter

indicators.note: the letters are filled by another piece put inside them
ultimately takes the last letter of Assistant

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: An assistant who ends up in charge is busy with work matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject or theme under discussion is the matter in hand.

clue.text: Theatrical entertainment overlong? Switch each half around

indicators.note: the two halves of the word overlong, over and long, trade places, so the O moves to the end

parts.note: read as two words: over is O, the cricket scorecard abbreviation, and long is pant, to yearn

explanation.surface: A complaint that a show runs too long, with a suggestion to reorder it.
explanation.walkthrough: PANTO is a British Christmas pantomime show. Read overlong as two words, over and long, and swap them.
explanation.definitionFit: The family Christmas stage show of slapstick and fairy tales is a theatrical entertainment.

clue.text: Mike indeed guards against losing extremely accommodating principal support

indicators.note: guards means these letters stand round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ay is an old word of assent, yes indeed

indicators.note: losing means the word against drops some letters
extremely means the outer letters of accommodating, its first and last

explanation.surface: Mike indeed defends against losing a very generous host.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely accommodating' gives A and G, which 'losing' takes from against to leave AINST, guarded by M and AY.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief prop or pillar of something, originally a ship's rope, is its key support.

clue.text: Swimmer runs to interrupt argument

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so this letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: a spat is a petty argument
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A swimmer races off to break up a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a person; it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A small herring-like fish of the sea is a creature that swims.

clue.text: Cease further trading, car's changing hands

indicators.note: changing hands means right is switched for left, R becoming L

parts.note: a Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: A dealer stops trading because a car has been sold to someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing hands' reads as a sale but means the right-hand letter R becomes the left-hand L.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that folds closes down for good, so it stops trading.

clue.text: Military equipment, single item I found buried in WWI battlefield

indicators.note: these letters are found buried inside the battlefield's name

parts.note: Mons in Belgium was the site of a famous 1914 battle
a unit is a single item

explanation.surface: A soldier's object found buried on a First World War battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: Shells, bombs and ammunition make up the stores of armed forces.

clue.text: Each time essentially Austrian's combating Nadal, providing close set

indicators.note: essentially means at the core, and each time applies it to every word in turn, taking the middle letters

explanation.surface: A tennis report: an Austrian fighting Nadal, as long as the set stays tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like a tennis set but is a wireless receiver.
explanation.definitionFit: A wireless receiving apparatus is called a set, as in a television or wireless set.

clue.text: Vessel damaged at the stern? In what way?

indicators.note: a ship's stern is its back, so this takes the last letter of damaged

parts.note: how asks in what way

explanation.surface: A boat is damaged at the back, and someone asks how.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab sailing boat with a lateen sail is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Visiting starved character, initially not seen without restraints

indicators.note: the letters visit, going inside the other word

parts.note: someone starved has gone unfed

indicators.note: initially not seen means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a letter is a written character

explanation.surface: Someone unseen at first, calling on a hungry figure, without restraints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially not seen' drops the opening L from the word for character, and 'Visiting' sends what remains inside the word for starved.
explanation.definitionFit: Free of shackles or chains, so not held back by any restriction.
